subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does Assessment Objective 1 (AO1) require candidates to do?
options: Develop ideas through investigations, demonstrating critical understanding of sources
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses
Present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions
Refine work by exploring ideas and experimenting with media
questions.explain: AO1 is about developing ideas through investigation and showing critical understanding of the sources studied.

questions.q: Which statement matches Assessment Objective 2 (AO2)?
options: Refine work by exploring ideas, selecting and experimenting with appropriate media, materials, techniques and processes
Develop ideas through investigations demonstrating critical understanding of sources
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions
Present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions
questions.explain: AO2 focuses on refining work through selecting and experimenting with media, materials, techniques and processes.

questions.q: Assessment Objective 3 (AO3) requires candidates to:
options: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses
Present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions
Refine work by experimenting with appropriate media and processes
Develop ideas through investigations demonstrating critical understanding
questions.explain: AO3 is about recording ideas, observations and insights that are relevant to intentions as the work develops.

questions.q: Which best describes Assessment Objective 4 (AO4)?
options: Present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions and, where appropriate, makes connections between visual and other elements
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses
Refine work by selecting and experimenting with appropriate media
Develop ideas through investigations demonstrating critical understanding of sources
questions.explain: AO4 is about presenting a personal, meaningful response that realises the candidate's intentions.

questions.q: How are the four assessment objectives weighted in AQA GCSE Art and Design?
options: Each objective carries equal weighting
AO1 and AO4 are weighted more heavily than AO2 and AO3
AO4 carries double the marks of the other objectives
AO1 carries the most marks as it comes first
questions.explain: All four assessment objectives are weighted equally in the qualification.

questions.q: What proportion of the total GCSE marks does Component 1 (Portfolio) contribute?
questions.explain: Component 1, the Portfolio, is worth 60% of the total GCSE, with Component 2 worth 40%.

questions.q: How many marks is Component 1 (Portfolio) worth?
options: 96 marks
48 marks
60 marks
120 marks
questions.explain: Component 1 is marked out of 96, with the four assessment objectives sharing these marks equally.

questions.q: In art and design research, what is a 'primary source'?
options: First-hand material the candidate observes or gathers themselves, such as their own photographs or objects
An image copied from a textbook
A reproduction of a famous painting found online
Written analysis provided by the teacher
questions.explain: Primary sources are first-hand, directly experienced material, unlike secondary sources such as books or the internet.

questions.q: A candidate tries the same design as a lino print, then as a watercolour, then as collage to decide which works best. Which AO is this chiefly evidencing?
options: AO2 (refining and experimenting with media)
AO1 (developing ideas from sources)
AO3 (recording observations)
AO4 (presenting a final response)
questions.explain: Experimenting with different media and techniques to refine work is the heart of AO2.

questions.q: Why does AO1 ask for 'critical understanding of sources' rather than simply copying an artist's work?
options: Candidates should analyse and respond to sources to inform their own developing ideas, not reproduce them
Copying is banned in all art examinations
Only photographs may be used as sources
Sources must always be modern artists
questions.explain: AO1 rewards critical engagement with sources that feeds a candidate's own idea development, not mere imitation.

questions.q: A candidate makes quick observational sketches and annotations noting how light falls on an object. Which AO does this most directly address?
options: AO3 (recording ideas, observations and insights)
AO1 (developing ideas from sources)
AO2 (refining through media experiments)
AO4 (presenting a personal response)
questions.explain: Observational recording and insight capture as work progresses is exactly what AO3 assesses.

questions.q: What does 'realises intentions' mean in the context of AO4?
options: The final response successfully achieves the aims the candidate set out to explore
The candidate realises they should change their whole topic
The work is completed within a strict time limit
The response copies the original artist exactly
questions.explain: Realising intentions means the resolved outcome fulfils the personal aims developed through the project.

questions.q: How should contextual research (studying other artists) best function within a portfolio?
options: As a stimulus that informs and drives the candidate's own developing ideas
As pages of copied images with no personal work
As a section completed only at the very end
As unrelated decoration between practical pieces
questions.explain: Contextual research is valued when it clearly influences and develops the candidate's personal ideas.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of annotation in a sketchbook or portfolio?
options: To record thinking, evaluate outcomes and explain how ideas are developing
To fill empty space so pages look full
To list the price of every material used
To copy the artist's biography word for word
questions.explain: Annotation evidences the candidate's reflective thinking and decision-making across the assessment objectives.

questions.q: Which pairing of assessment objective and key word is correct?
options: AO2 - Refine
AO2 - Present
AO1 - Record
AO3 - Develop
questions.explain: The key words are AO1 Develop, AO2 Refine, AO3 Record and AO4 Present.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of gathering a primary source?
options: Photographing a landscape yourself to draw from later
Downloading another artist's painting from a museum website
Printing an image from a search engine
Tracing a picture from a magazine
questions.explain: Taking your own photographs is first-hand, primary-source gathering, whereas downloaded images are secondary.

questions.q: A candidate produces a resolved final outcome that deliberately draws together ideas, media and imagery explored earlier in the project. Which AO is best evidenced?
options: AO4 (presenting a personal and meaningful response)
AO1 (developing ideas)
AO2 (refining media)
AO3 (recording observations)
questions.explain: A resolved final piece that connects earlier development into a meaningful outcome addresses AO4.

questions.q: As a project develops, a candidate keeps written and visual notes on what is working and why, adjusting plans accordingly. This most clearly demonstrates:
options: AO3 (recording ideas and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses)
AO4 (presenting a final response)
AO1 (critical understanding of sources)
AO2 (experimenting with new media)
questions.explain: Ongoing recording of insights relevant to intentions is precisely the focus of AO3.

questions.q: A candidate visits a gallery, photographs a painting and writes an analysis of its composition and colour to feed into their own project. Which AO does this best serve?
options: AO1 (developing ideas through investigation and critical understanding of sources)
AO2 (refining through media experiments)
AO3 (recording observations only)
AO4 (presenting the final response)
questions.explain: Investigating and critically analysing a source to inform ideas is the essence of AO1.

questions.q: A candidate has strong idea development, good media experiments and detailed recording, but never produces a resolved outcome. Which AO is most likely to score poorly?
options: AO4 (present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions)
AO1 (develop ideas)
AO2 (refine work)
AO3 (record observations)
questions.explain: Without a resolved final outcome, AO4, which rewards presenting a response that realises intentions, will be weak.

specSource: AQA GCSE Art and Design specification; Component 1: Portfolio (Personal Investigation)
